Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 88, verse 1–7:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿Has there come to you the news of the Overwhelming (al-Ghashiyah)? Faces that Day will be humbled, labouring and weary, burning in a scorching fire, given to drink from a boiling spring. For them there is no food except from a thorny plant, which neither nourishes nor satisfies hunger.﴾

His, may He be remembered, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: ﴿Has there come to you﴾ O Muhammad ﴿the news of the Overwhelming﴾, meaning: its story and report.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning the meaning of al-Ghashiyah. Some of them said: It is the Resurrection, which overwhelms people with its terrors.

Mention of those who said that:

Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿al-Ghashiyah﴾ is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection, which God magnified and warned His servants of.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: ﴿Has there come to you the news of the Overwhelming﴾, he said: al-Ghashiyah is the Hour.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words: ﴿Has there come to you the news of the Overwhelming﴾, he said: the Hour.

Others said: Rather, al-Ghashiyah is the Fire, which overwhelms the faces of the disbelievers.

Mention of those who said that:

Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Yaman related to us, from Ashath, from Sa'id, concerning His words: ﴿Has there come to you the news of the Overwhelming﴾, he said: the overwhelming of the Fire.

The correct view on this matter is to say: God said to His Prophet ﷺ: ﴿Has there come to you the news of the Overwhelming﴾; He did not inform us that He meant the overwhelming of the Resurrection, nor that He meant the overwhelming of the Fire. Both are an overwhelming: this one overwhelms people with trials, terrors and distresses, and that one overwhelms the disbelievers with the scorching of the faces, the blaze and molten brass. There is no statement on this more sound than to say as He, may His praise be exalted, said, and to let the report encompass that just as He encompassed it.

* *

His words: ﴿Faces that Day will be humbled﴾

He, may He be remembered, says: faces on that Day, and they are the faces of those who disbelieved in Him, ﴿humbled﴾, meaning: abased.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, ﴿Faces that Day will be humbled﴾: i.e., abased.

Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, concerning His words: ﴿humbled﴾, he said: humbled in the Fire.

* *

His words: ﴿labouring﴾

Meaning: labouring in the Fire.

* *

His words: ﴿and weary﴾

He says: weary therein.

The people of interpretation said similarly to what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning ﴿labouring and weary﴾: they labour and are wearied by the Fire.

Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah related to us, from Abu Raja', who said: I heard al-Hasan recite ﴿labouring and weary﴾, and he said: They did not labour for God in the world, so they are made to labour in the Fire.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, ﴿labouring and weary﴾: they were arrogant in the world toward obedience to God, so they are made to labour and be wearied in the Fire.

Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, concerning His words: ﴿labouring and weary﴾, he said: labouring and weary in the Fire.

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: ﴿labouring and weary﴾: None is more wearied nor more severely afflicted than the people of the Fire.

* *

His words: ﴿burning in a scorching fire﴾

He, may He be remembered, says: these faces will be brought to a scorching fire, heated and its heat intensified.

The reciters differed in reading this. The common reciters of Kufa read ﴿tasla﴾ with an open "t", meaning: the faces are burned (tasla al-wujuh). Abu 'Amr read ﴿tusla﴾ with a dammed "t", considering His words ﴿they are given to drink from a boiling spring﴾. The view on this is that both are readings sound in meaning, and whichever of them the reciter reads, he is correct.

* *

His words: ﴿given to drink from a boiling spring﴾

He says: the people of these faces are given to drink from the drink of a spring whose heat has reached its limit, attaining the utmost intensity of heat.

The people of interpretation said similarly to what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words: ﴿given to drink from a boiling spring﴾, he said: It is the one whose groaning has been prolonged.

Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah related to us, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan, concerning His words: ﴿given to drink from a boiling spring﴾, he said: Its cooking has been going on since the day God created the world.

Others said: What is meant by His words ﴿from a boiling spring﴾ is from a present spring.

Mention of those who said that:

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: ﴿given to drink from a boiling spring﴾, he said: "boiling" (ani): present.

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Layth, from Mujahid, the same.

Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words ﴿ḍarī‘﴾, he said: dried al-shibriq.

Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, ﴿except from a thorny plant﴾, he said: it is al-shibriq when it dries, called ḍarī‘.

Muhammad ibn Ubayd related to me, saying: Sharik ibn Abd Allah related to us, concerning His words: (For them there is no food except from a thorny plant), he said: al-shibriq.

Others said: al-ḍarī‘ is stones.

Mention of those who said that:

Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Yaman related to us, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, concerning His words: ﴿For them there is no food except from a thorny plant﴾, he said: stones.

Others said: al-ḍarī‘ is a tree of fire.

Mention of those who said that:

Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words: ﴿For them there is no food except from a thorny plant﴾, he says: a tree of fire.

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: ﴿For them there is no food except from a thorny plant﴾, he said: al-ḍarī‘ is the thorn of fire. On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Faces that Day will be joyful,﴾ [8] ﴿pleased with their striving,﴾ [9] ﴿in a lofty Garden,﴾ [10] ﴿wherein they will hear no idle talk.﴾ [11] ﴿Therein is a flowing spring,﴾ [12] ﴿therein are raised couches,﴾ [13] ﴿and cups set in place,﴾ [14] ﴿and cushions lined up,﴾ [15] ﴿and carpets spread out.﴾ [16]

His exalted remembrance says: ﴿Faces that Day﴾ means: on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿joyful﴾ means: they are joyful through the bounty God bestows on their people in His Gardens, and they are the people of faith in God.

* *

And His saying: ﴿pleased with their striving﴾

means: pleased with their deeds which they performed in the world by obeying their Lord. It has also been said that ﴿pleased with their striving﴾ means: pleased with the reward of their striving in the Hereafter.

* *

And His saying: ﴿in a lofty Garden﴾

It is a garden, ﴿lofty﴾ meaning: elevated.

* *

And His saying: ﴿wherein they will hear no idle talk﴾

means: these faces will not hear idle talk (al-laghiyah) in it, meaning: their people therein, in the lofty Garden. By al-laghiyah is meant a word of lagha (vain talk), and lagha means falsehood; so the word that is lagha is called laghiyah, just as the wearer of a coat of mail is called dari' (armored), the owner of a horse fari (horseman), and the one who recites poetry shā'ir (poet), and as al-Hutay'ah said:

"You deceived me and claimed that you are a possessor of milk in summer, a possessor of dates..."

meaning: a possessor of milk and a possessor of dates. Some of the Kufans claimed that the meaning of this is: "You will not hear in it one who swears falsely, and therefore it is called laghiyah." What he said has a basis and a line of argument, were it not that the people of interpretation among the Companions and the Successors are in disagreement with it, and it is not permissible for anyone to oppose them in what they were unanimous upon.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said on this point.

His exalted remembrance says: ﴿Faces that Day﴾ means: on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿joyful﴾ means: they are joyful through the bounty God bestows on their people in His Gardens, and they are the people of faith in God.

* *

And His saying: ﴿pleased with their striving﴾

means: pleased with their deeds which they performed in the world by obeying their Lord. It has also been said that ﴿pleased with their striving﴾ means: pleased with the reward of their striving in the Hereafter.

* *

And His saying: ﴿in a lofty Garden﴾

It is a garden, ﴿lofty﴾ meaning: elevated.

* *

And His saying: ﴿wherein they will hear no idle talk﴾

means: these faces will not hear idle talk (al-laghiyah) in it, meaning: their people therein, in the lofty Garden. By al-laghiyah is meant a word of lagha (vain talk), and lagha means falsehood; so the word that is lagha is called laghiyah, just as the wearer of a coat of mail is called dari' (armored), the owner of a horse fari (horseman), and the one who recites poetry shā'ir (poet), and as al-Hutay'ah said:

"You deceived me and claimed that you are a possessor of milk in summer, a possessor of dates..."

meaning: a possessor of milk and a possessor of dates. Some of the Kufans claimed that the meaning of this is: "You will not hear in it one who swears falsely, and therefore it is called laghiyah." What he said has a basis and a line of argument, were it not that the people of interpretation among the Companions and the Successors are in disagreement with it, and it is not permissible for anyone to oppose them in what they were unanimous upon.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said on this point.

Mention of those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿wherein they will hear no idle talk﴾: he said: they will not hear harm or falsehood.

* Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, he said: Abu Asim related to us, he said: Isa related to us, and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿wherein they will hear no idle talk﴾, he said: insult.

* Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿wherein they will hear no idle talk﴾: they will not hear falsehood or insult therein.

* Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, the like of that.

The readers differed in the recitation of this. The majority of the readers of Kufa and some readers of Medina, namely Abu Ja'far, recited ﴿lā tasma'u﴾ with a fatha on the ta', meaning: the faces do not hear. Ibn Kathir, Nafi' and Abu Amr recited ﴿lā tusma'u﴾ with a damma on the ta', in the passive form, and the feminine ending on tasma' is due to the feminine noun laghiyah. Ibn Muhaysin also recited it with a damma, except that he read it with a ya' in the masculine form.

The correct position in this matter, in my view, is that all of these are well-known recitations with sound meanings, so whichever reading the reciter uses, he is correct.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Therein is a flowing spring﴾

means: in the lofty Garden is a flowing spring, not in a trench.

* *

And His saying: ﴿therein are raised couches﴾

The plural of sarir (couch) is surur. ﴿Raised﴾ so that the believer, when he sits upon them, sees all that his Lord has granted him of bounty and dominion therein, and all of that reaches his sight.

It has been said that by ﴿raised﴾ is meant ﴿mawdunah﴾ (interwoven/woven together).

Mention of those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿therein are raised couches﴾, he said: meaning woven together, like His saying: "couches arranged, one above another."

* *

And His saying: ﴿and cups set in place﴾

They are the plural of kub, which are the ewers without handles. We have clarified this earlier and mentioned the reports concerning it, sufficient to not repeat it.

By His saying ﴿set in place﴾ is meant that they are placed on the brink of the flowing spring, so that whenever they wish to drink they find them full of drink.

* *

And His saying: ﴿and cushions lined up﴾

By namariq is meant cushions and armrests. The singular of namariq is numruqah, with a damma on the nun. It has been related from some of the Banu Kalb, by hearing, numriqah, with a kasra on the nun and the ra'. It has been said: lined up, because some of them are beside others.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said on this point.

Mention of those who said that:

* Ali related to me, he said: Abu Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿and cushions lined up﴾: he said: armrests.

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿and cushions lined up﴾, he said: by namariq is meant the gatherings (majalis).

* Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿and cushions lined up﴾: namariq are the cushions.

* *

And His saying: ﴿and carpets spread out﴾

His exalted remembrance says: therein are many rugs and spreads, spread out, and the singular is zirbiyyah, which is a rug with a fine soft pile.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said on this point.

Mention of those who said that:

* Ahmad ibn Mansur related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Sufyan, he said: Tawbah al-Anbari related to us, from Ikrimah ibn Khalid, from Abdullah ibn Ammar, who said: I saw Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) pray on a 'abqari, which is the zarabi.

* Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and carpets spread out﴾: spread out.

The Interpretation of His, the Exalted's, Words: "Do they not look at the camels, how they were created? And at the sky, how it was raised? And at the mountains, how they were set up? And at the earth, how it was spread out?" (88:17–20)

Says God, exalted is His mention, to those who deny His power over what He described in this surah of punishment and retribution which He has prepared for the people of His enmity, and of bliss and honor which He has prepared for the people of His allegiance: "Do not these deniers look at God's power over these matters? [Look] at the camels, how He created them, subjected them for them, made them docile, and made them carry their burden while kneeling, then rise with it. He who created that is not unable to create what has been described of these matters in Paradise and Hell." Says He, majestic is His praise: "Do they not look at the camels so that they may take warning from them, and know that the power by which He has determined to create them will not fail Him to create what resembles them?"

Ahl al-ta'wil (the people of interpretation) have said the like of what we have said about this.

Those who said so:

Basharun narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: When God described what is in Paradise, the people of misguidance marveled at that, so God revealed: "Do they not look at the camels, how they were created?" The camels were then among the sustenance of the Arabs and among their livestock.

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from one who heard Shurayh say: "Come out with us, let us look at the camels, how they were created."

* *

As for His saying: "And at the sky, how it was raised"

Says He, exalted is His praise: "Do they not also look at the sky, how He raised it, He who informed you that He has prepared for His friends what has been described, and for His enemies what has been mentioned, so that they may know that His power is such that doing anything He wills is not beyond Him."

* *

As for His saying: "And at the mountains, how they were set up"

Says [He]: And at the mountains, how they were erected upright, not collapsing so as to spread out over the earth, but He made them upright and firm by His power, not leaving their place nor departing from their position.

And Basharun narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: "And at the mountains, how they were set up": Ascend the mountain Sayhud all day long; when you reach its top, you will arrive at gushing springs and drooping fruits, which no hands have ploughed or worked, a blessing from God and a provision for a term.

* *

As for His saying: "And at the earth, how it was spread out"

Says [He]: And at the earth, how it was spread out. It is said: "a mountain that is musattah" when there is levelness at its summit.

Ahl al-ta'wil have said the like of what we have said about this.

**The discussion of the interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying, exalted is He:** ﴿So remind, for you are only one who reminds. You are not over them a controller. Except for one who turns away and disbelieves. Then Allah will punish him with the greatest punishment. Indeed, to Us is their return. Then indeed, upon Us is their account.﴾

God, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: ﴿So remind﴾, O Muhammad, My servants with My signs, admonish them with My proofs, and convey My message to them. ﴿For you are only one who reminds﴾ means: I have sent you to them only as a reminder, so that you may remind them of My blessings upon them, make known to them what they are obligated to, and admonish them.

* *

And His saying: ﴿You are not over them a controller﴾

Meaning: you are not over them one who has authority, nor are you a tyrant who compels them to do what you want. It means: leave them to Me, leave them and My judgment concerning them. It is said: "So-and-so has become a controller (musaytir) over his people" when he has become dominant over them.

Those who gave interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said the same as what we have said about this.

He said: then after this came: ﴿Strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be harsh with them﴾, and He said: ﴿Sit in wait for them at every place of ambush﴾, and: ﴿watch them so that they do not go out into the land﴾, and ﴿If they repent, establish prayer, and give zakah, then let them go their way; indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. He said: so ﴿You are not over them a controller﴾ was abrogated. He said: [the command was]: "Fight them until he is killed or embraces Islam." He said: but the reminder remains as it is, not abrogated, and he recited: ﴿And remind, for the reminder benefits the believers﴾.

When they say: There is no god but Allah, they have protected their blood and their property from me, except by its right, and their account is with Allah." Then he recited: ﴿Indeed, you are only one who reminds, you are not over them a controller﴾.

* Yusuf ibn Musa al-Qattan narrated to us, he said: Waki narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the like of it.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Except one who turns away and disbelieves﴾

This may be understood in two ways. The first: remind your people, O Muhammad, except those among them who turn away from you and turn aside from the signs of Allah and disbelieve. Then the word "except" (illa) is an exception from those upon whom the reminder was directed, even though they did not receive it, as one says: "So-and-so passed by and called [people], except those whose response is not hoped for," meaning: he called the people, except those whose response is not hoped for. The second way: to take His saying: ﴿Except one who turns away and disbelieves﴾ as disconnected from what precedes it, so that the meaning of the speech becomes: you are not over them a controller, except that whoever turns away and disbelieves, Allah will punish him. The disconnected exception (al-istithna al-munqati) is tested by whether inna (indeed) can appropriately precede it: if it can, the exception is disconnected; if it cannot, the exception is a proper connected exception, as in the saying of the speaker: "The people traveled, except Zayd," where inna cannot appropriately be inserted here, because this is a proper exception.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Then Allah will punish him with the greatest punishment﴾

This is the punishment of Hell. The meaning: Allah will punish him with the greatest punishment for his disbelief in the world, and the punishment of Hell in the Hereafter.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, to Us is their return﴾

Meaning: indeed, to Us is the return and the resurrection of those who disbelieved. ﴿Then indeed, upon Us is their account﴾ means: then indeed, upon Allah is their account, and He will recompense them for what they committed of disobedience to their Lord. By this He informs His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ that He is the one who takes charge of their punishment, not him; He is the one who recompenses and punishes, and that the reminder and conveyance of the message is incumbent upon him.

Those who gave interpretation said the same as what we have said about this.

* Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿Indeed, to Us is their return, then indeed, upon Us is their account﴾, meaning: indeed, to Allah is the return, and upon Him is the account.

Then he recited: ﴿Indeed, you are only one who reminds, you are not over them a controller﴾.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu al-Zubayr Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I heard Jabir ibn Abd Allah say: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say, and he mentioned the like of it, except that he said: Abu al-Zubayr said: then he recited: ﴿Indeed, you are only one who reminds, you are not over them a controller﴾.

* Yusuf ibn Musa al-Qattan narrated to us, he said: Waki narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the like of it.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Except one who turns away and disbelieves﴾

This may be understood in two ways. The first: remind your people, O Muhammad, except those among them who turn away from you and turn aside from the signs of Allah and disbelieve. Then the word "except" (illa) is an exception from those upon whom the reminder was directed, even though they did not receive it, as one says: "So-and-so passed by and called [people], except those whose response is not hoped for," meaning: he called the people, except those whose response is not hoped for. The second way: to take His saying: ﴿Except one who turns away and disbelieves﴾ as disconnected from what precedes it, so that the meaning of the speech becomes: you are not over them a controller, except that whoever turns away and disbelieves, Allah will punish him. The disconnected exception (al-istithna al-munqati) is tested by whether inna (indeed) can appropriately precede it: if it can, the exception is disconnected; if it cannot, the exception is a proper connected exception, as in the saying of the speaker: "The people traveled, except Zayd," where inna cannot appropriately be inserted here, because this is a proper exception.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Then Allah will punish him with the greatest punishment﴾

This is the punishment of Hell. The meaning: Allah will punish him with the greatest punishment for his disbelief in the world, and the punishment of Hell in the Hereafter.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, to Us is their return﴾

Meaning: indeed, to Us is the return and the resurrection of those who disbelieved. ﴿Then indeed, upon Us is their account﴾ means: then indeed, upon Allah is their account, and He will recompense them for what they committed of disobedience to their Lord. By this He informs His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ that He is the one who takes charge of their punishment, not him; He is the one who recompenses and punishes, and that the reminder and conveyance of the message is incumbent upon him.

Those who gave interpretation said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu Asim narrated to us, he said: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿Except one who turns away and disbelieves﴾, he said: his account is with Allah.

* Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿Indeed, to Us is their return, then indeed, upon Us is their account﴾, meaning: indeed, to Allah is the return, and upon Him is the account.

**The end of the tafsir (commentary) of Surah al-Ghashiya.**
